title: Find and Verify Work Emails at Scale (Waterfall, 0 Credits on Misses)
summary: How go-to-market teams and their coding agents find and verify work emails for a whole list with Cargo: one batch call per provider, cheapest first, misses free, then one verify call. With Cargo platform data on hit rates and cost.
body_markdown:
**To find and verify work emails for a go-to-market list, run one Cargo batch call per email provider over your rows, cheapest provider first and only the misses passed on, then one verify call over the emails you found. A miss costs 0 credits, so you pay only for emails found and addresses checked.**


No Hunter, Prospeo or FullEnrich account is needed: Cargo calls each provider on its own key and bills credits. The steps below are the[find-work-email](https://www.getcargo.ai/skills/find-work-email) and[verify-email-list](https://www.getcargo.ai/skills/verify-email-list) skills, end to end, with the fields each provider returns.


## What 1.57M find-email runs show#


Cargo platform data, 90 days to Oct 16 2026:


Measure Value


Find-email runs about 1.57M, across 800+ workspaces


Runs that returned an email 64%


Credits charged on not-found results 0, across about 1.0M empty provider lookups


Found rate, runs chaining 4 or more providers 90% (97,640 runs)


Found rate, single-provider runs 66% (1.14M runs)


One run can try several providers, which is why empty provider lookups outnumber runs that found nothing. The waterfall gap is correlational: the two groups ran on different lists, so it is not a controlled test of the same contacts. It is still the clearest reason to chain providers rather than pick one.


What a found email costs, per provider, from each action’s credit definition:


Provider Credits per found email


Icypeas 0.1


Findymail, Prospeo, Hunter 0.5


FullEnrich, Dropcontact, Enrow, Datagma 1


A new account starts with 100 free credits and no card, which covers, for example, 200 emails found on Prospeo or Hunter, or 1,000 on Icypeas.


## Run it#


### 1. Install and sign in


shellscript


```text
npm   install   -g   @cargo-ai/cli
cargo-ai   login   --email   you@company.com                   # sends a code
cargo-ai   login   --email   you@company.com   --code   123456     # creates the account on first use


```


There is no browser step, so a coding agent can run this itself. Signed-out catalog browsing and free dry runs are coming to the CLI; today, the sign-up above is the way in.


### 2. Find the actions


shellscript


```text
cargo-ai   orchestration   action   list   find   email
cargo-ai   orchestration   action   list   verify   email


```


Each result carries an` action` object to pass to the next command and a` credits` array with its price. Nothing runs and nothing is charged. The examples below leave out the` connectorUuid` that object may carry, in which case Cargo uses the workspace’s default connector for that provider.


### 3. Pilot the first rung on 5 rows


Start with the cheapest provider.` --limit 5` submits only the first five records, so you can read the output and the cost before the full run.


shellscript


```text
cargo-ai   orchestration   action   execute-batch   \
--action   '{"kind":"connector","integrationSlug":"icypeas","actionSlug":"findEmail"}'   \
--records   '[{"firstName":"Ada","lastName":"Lovelace","domainOrCompany":"example.com"}]'   \
--limit   5   --wait-until-finished


```


### 4. Run the full list, then escalate only the misses


Drop` --limit` to run every row. Download the results with` cargo-ai orchestration batch download --uuid <batch uuid>` , keep the rows that came back without an email, and send those to the next provider. Each provider names its inputs differently:


Rung Action Credits Record fields


1` icypeas.findEmail` 0.1` firstName` ,` lastName` ,` domainOrCompany`


2` prospeo.findEmail` 0.5` firstName` ,` lastName` ,` companyDomain`


3` hunter.findEmail` 0.5` first_name` ,` last_name` ,` domain`


4` FullEnrich.findEmail` 1` firstName` ,` lastName` ,` domainName`


shellscript


```text
# Rung 4, on the rows rungs 1 to 3 missed
cargo-ai   orchestration   action   execute-batch   \
--action   '{"kind":"connector","integrationSlug":"FullEnrich","actionSlug":"findEmail"}'   \
--records   "$(  cat   misses.json)"   \
--wait-until-finished


```


Never send the full list to every rung: the found emails are already paid for, and a second provider charges again for the same person.


### 5. Verify what you found


shellscript


```text
cargo-ai   orchestration   action   execute-batch   \
--action   '{"kind":"connector","integrationSlug":"waterfall","actionSlug":"verifyEmail"}'   \
--records   '[{"email":"ada@example.com"}]'   \
--wait-until-finished


```


` waterfall.verifyEmail` (Waterfall.io) costs 0.1 credits per address and, unlike a finder, charges for every address it checks. Other verifiers in the catalog: ZeroBounce (0.1), NeverBounce (0.2), Findymail (0.25), Bouncer (0.3) and Hunter (1). Verify even when the finder sent its own status: a finder grading its own result is not an independent check.


## What comes back#


Each finder returns the provider’s own record. The fields to read:


Action Email Confidence or status


` icypeas.findEmail`` emails\[\].email`` emails\[\].certainty` , plus` mxProvider`


` prospeo.findEmail`` person.email.email` Prospeo’s email object, returned as Prospeo sends it


` hunter.findEmail`` email`` score` ,` accept_all` (catch-all domain),` verification.status`


` FullEnrich.findEmail`` most_probable_email`` most_probable_email_status` , and` emails\[\].status` for every candidate


` findyMail.findEmail`` email` none beyond the address


` waterfall.verifyEmail`` email`` email_status` (` valid` when deliverable),` smtp_provider` ,` mx_records`


A not-found row comes back with no data and is not charged.` cargo-ai orchestration action get-output-schema --action '<action object>'` prints any action’s output schema without running it.


## Frequently asked questions#


No. Unless you connect your own key, Cargo calls the provider on Cargo’s key and bills the action’s credits. If you already pay a provider, you can connect your key instead.


No. A find-email action that returns no email returns no data, and no credits are charged. Across about 1.0M empty provider lookups in the 90 days to Oct 16 2026, 0 credits were charged. Verification is different: waterfall.verifyEmail charges for every address it checks.


Coverage differs by provider, region and company. In Cargo platform data for the 90 days to Oct 16 2026, runs that chained four or more providers found an email 90% of the time, against 66% for single-provider runs. The lists differed, so this is a correlation rather than a controlled test.


A new account gets 100 free credits with no card. At 0.5 credits per found email on Prospeo or Hunter, that is 200 found emails; at 0.1 on Icypeas, it is 1,000.
